cards.name: retune-the-launcher-per-m-bucket-before-touching-an-elementwise-fp8-group-quant-body
cards.description: Per-M-bucket BLOCK_SIZE_N/num_warps table on a fused SiLU-mul + per-1x128 fp8 group-quant Triton prologue: 2.06x geomean, kernel body byte-identical
cards.key: fused SiLU-mul + dynamic per-1x128 fp8 group-quant prologue (aiter Triton) on gfx950, one dispatch, decode and prefill M buckets scored under a fixed measurement window
cards.title: Retune the launcher per M bucket before touching an element-wise fp8 group-quant body
cards.effect: 2.06x director-verified unweighted geomean vs the frozen baseline, parity bit-identical (err=0 on all five legs). The launcher table alone carries the whole run: elements-per-lane 0.5 -> 8.0, VALU-per-element 6.3x lower, kernel device time 4.96x faster at prefill and 1.93x at decode, with the kernel body byte-identical to the golden. Two further rounds (about 100 body variants) produced real device-time wins (up to -11% prefill) and none cleared the scoring noise floor.
cards.roofline: both buckets VALU-issue bound before; after, the bound SPLITS - prefill stays compute-bound (VALU ~0.95 of CU-busy) and simultaneously reaches ~0.63 of HBM peak, decode leaves the compute regime (VALU ~0.39, HBM ~0.19) into GPU-fill/issue-wait with ~1.1 average resident waves per SIMD. Zero-cost-kernel ceiling is ~2.15x weighted and the incumbent already sits at ~0.99 of it.
cards.lever: On an element-wise quant-cast fused into an activation, spend the first direction on a per-M-bucket launch table (BLOCK_SIZE_N x num_warps x waves_per_eu x num_stages), not on the body: a stock launcher that gives well under one element per lane makes every wave pay a fixed ~50-instruction prologue, and buying elements-per-lane back is worth more than any instruction-count edit that follows.
cards.apply: Host/wrapper-only edit: bucket M at dispatch into a config table (here decode BLOCK_SIZE_N=512 / 1 warp, prefill 1024 / 2 warps, waves_per_eu=0, num_stages=1) and keep the compiled body byte-identical, so parity risk is near zero. Register each arm under its own symbol, gate it on its table row plus a proved-safe shape predicate, early-return before the stock dispatch, and add NO catch-all default.
cards.verify: Frozen-baseline isolated A/B per bucket plus oracle parity on every leg, and confirm each bucket actually resolves to its own row. Judge candidates on profiler dispatch durations, not on the scored ratio: the harness compresses a device win by about 3x at decode and 2x at prefill, so a decode direction needs a >5% device win to be visible at all. Re-read the bottleneck split after every config change - it is a property of the config, not of the source.
cards.pitfall:
A config read as the fastest in a raw sweep but was silently wrong -> BLOCK_SIZE_N=2048 does not divide N_half=17408 (8.5 tiles), so the grid truncated and the EVEN_N path broke -> require the block to divide the row, and check the parity error before the time on every sweep row.
The entry profile showed both buckets issue-saturated and sent two rounds after instruction count -> its 'per-SIMD' VALU utilisation divided total VALU cycles by CU count on a 4-SIMD-per-CU part, so it read ~4x high -> classify the regime from convention-free per-wave counters (VALU per wave, waves launched vs resident), never from a utilisation percentage whose denominator you did not check.
A merged candidate read +0.75% and re-measured at -0.01% against the same incumbent -> the verifier scores one rep per case with zero spread, so promotion rode a single draw of a process whose own run-to-run spread is the size of every remaining effect -> decide promotion with an interleaved multi-rep A/B against a paired control, never one verify draw.
A 50-launch graph chain used to rank variants mis-ranked them -> back-to-back graph nodes overlap, so it reported a much shorter time than the true dispatch duration and compressed the spread -> rank on profiler dispatch durations and use the graph chain only to measure the dispatch floor.
Taking a baseline control by reverting the kernel source aborted the run -> the pseudo-identity guard rejects an unchanged source -> check the committed patch out into a separate workspace, git init and commit the canonical source there, and verify the patch applies standalone.
cards.caution: Also price the fixed measurement window before funding any body direction: here candidate device time plus a constant predicted the scored number within 4% in both buckets, ~75% of the scored decode number was window and a further large share per-dispatch floor, so the addressable fraction was under a tenth of the score. Also verify occupancy hints per bucket - waves_per_eu>0 cost about 4% at decode but two orders of magnitude at prefill, and an N-major launch grid removed the need for the hint entirely.
